root_idea.summary: The root centers on something reaching its seeker only with difficulty, hardness, or impediment.
root_idea.development: From difficult attainment or emergence, the lexical range extends to scant or exhausted supply, withholding, hardship, distress, and adverse effects. These root-level developments are broader than the single Quranic nominal occurrence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized adjective citation form نَكِدٌ rather than the accusative Quranic surface form نَكِدًا.

senses.definition: Hard to obtain; coming forth only with difficulty.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction وَالَّذِي خَبُثَ لَا يَخْرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِدًا, it describes something that emerges only with difficulty.

senses.definition: Scanty or unprofitable in what it yields.
senses.usage_conditions: In the same Quranic construction, the sense focuses on emergence in a scant amount or without useful result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hard, straitened, or difficult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of a person's life and, more broadly, of becoming difficult or constrained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become deficient, scant, or exhausted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of milk, water, or a well whose available supply becomes little or runs out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become unpropitious, mean, hard, or difficult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person characterized by an adverse or unyielding disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold or refuse what someone asks, giving little or nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use with a requested need or object; it may also describe someone who has many askers but gives little.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a raven or crow, to croak with its utmost force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the bird's loud, strained croaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impair or diminish a gift by reproach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of giving that is spoiled by accompanying it with reproach or reminders of the favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spend or exhaust one's possessions through repeated petitions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes resources depleted as a result of frequent requests.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vex, distress, or trouble someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat someone with hardness, harshness, or ill nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or interpersonal Form III construction directed toward another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prove hard, mean, or niggardly to someone making a request.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when a person asks for a need or seeks something and the person asked yields only scantily.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vexed, distressed, or troubled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive or reflexive Form V use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat each other with hardness, harshness, or ill nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The scantiness of a gift and its being unenjoyable or unpleasant to its recipient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of a deficient or unwelcome gift.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imprecation wishing straitness, difficulty, or poverty on someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in formulas of malediction or adverse invocation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything that brings evil upon the person whom it affects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of an adverse influence or outcome.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, straitened, or difficult, of life or fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to difficult circumstances or adverse fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scant in quantity, of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use for a small available quantity of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unpropitious, mean, hard, or harmful person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description may denote someone difficult or unyielding, or someone who brings evil upon others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hardness or difficulty in a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of a person's difficult or harsh character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land possessing little in the way of goods or resources.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of lands or regions with scant produce or possessions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel described in conflicting ways as abundant in milk because she has no living young to suckle, or as having no or little milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also refer to a she-camel whose young has died; the lexicographical descriptions preserve these opposing applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unfortunate or unlucky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of adverse fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small or scanty gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of a gift that is little in amount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who gives little despite having many petitioners, or who is pressed by petitions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person characterized by scant giving under repeated requests.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unwelcome or empty in one's coming to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in the expression جَاءَهُ مُنْكِدًا; an alternative reading and derivation is also reported for this expression.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Exhausted water is covered by the deficient-or-exhausted supply meaning.
A well with little water is covered by the same supply meaning.
Contains both the hard or unpropitious disposition and niggardly withholding branches.
Giving only the least of what was requested.
Having many askers and giving little.
Proving hard or niggardly to a requester.
Requesting a need and receiving niggardly treatment.
Anything bringing evil to its recipient.
Quran-attested difficulty and scant or unprofitable emergence.
A person who brings evil is covered by the broader person-description meaning.
Hardness or difficulty in a person.
Blank lexical pointer fragment with no recoverable definition.
Person giving little under repeated petitions.
Reported unwelcome or empty arrival use.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested only at 7:58:12. Its two listed senses preserve the distinct lexical interpretations of difficulty and scant or unprofitable emergence; no additional modern Quran location is inferred from historical citation notation.
The Classical description of نَكْدَاءُ is internally conflicting: it is variously associated with abundant milk, absent or little milk, and the death of the young.

The interpretation of مُنْكِدًا in جَاءَهُ مُنْكِدًا is accompanied by an alternative reading and derivational correction; the reported lexical interpretation is retained without treating the correction as a separate form.
